newsitem.title: ROMANIA: Two more stocks to join Bucharest bourse.
newsitem.headline: Two more stocks to join Bucharest bourse.

text.p: The Bucharest stock exchange said on Wednesday two more companies would join in trading next week bringing to 19 the number of traded stocks.

A bourse statement said shares in state-run companies Carbochim SA, a steam generator manufacturer, and Feleacul SA, a confectionery maker, would start being traded on the exchange's second tier on February 11.
Carbochim, based in the Transylvanian city of Cluj, has a share capital of 34.3 billion lei, or some 1.4 million shares with a face value of 25,000 lei each.

Both Carbochim and Feleacul were included in a 1995 mass selloff scheme offering Romanians stakes of up to 60 percent in 4,000 companies in exchange for coupons. Subscription was 24 percent for Carbochim and 29 percent for Feleacul.
Carbochim's majority stockholder is the State Owernship Fuind (FPS) with a 54 percent stake. A private ownership fund has 14 percent and employees hold 8.0 percent.
Feleacul, based also in Cluj, has a share capital of 6.2 billion lei and its shares have a nominal value of 1,000 lei each. The FPS holds 51 percent of the company and enployees have 20 percent.
Brokers hailed the newcomers as adding to bourse liquidity. "That's what we are waiting for - more stocks to boost liquidity and offer investors a wider choice," said one.
The exchange now trades 17 stocks, of which only one -- fertiliser maker Azomures SA -- is listed on its first tier, where qualification criteria are tougher.
Bourse activity, which has been dull for the most part of 1996, turned buoyant this year, with volumes and most prices on the rise since early January.
Traders said the change of trend was mainly a result of growing interest in Romanian equities from local institutional investors and forerign buyers.
"With the new government pledging support to capital market growth, these investors are now looking at Romanian stocks with greater confidence," a trader said.
Romania is now ruled by a centrist coalition, which ousted leftists in general elections last November.

"I'm very optimistic about the Bucharest stock exchange because the way I see it the liquidity will improve as more companies come to the market," ING Barings analyst Mark Holdsworth said from London.
The bourse said another 12 companies had won a quotation and would soon join in trading. More than 50 companies have applied for a listing, it said. -- Luli Popescu, Bucharest Newsroom 40-1 3120264
